zones.name: Pagewood School
zones.intro: The village storybook is missing seven sun pages. Its first page is hiding in a very small word: hello.

quests.title: A little hello
quests.brief: Help Nắng welcome the new neighbors.

questions.prompt: A new neighbor says: “Hi, I’m Nắng.” What do you say?
questions.note: “Nice to meet you” is a friendly first greeting.

questions.prompt: Introduce yourself to your neighbor.
questions.note: Use “My name is…” to introduce yourself.

questions.prompt: Nắng asks, “How are you?” Choose a natural reply.
questions.note: Answer how you feel, then thank the person.

quests.title: The first sun page
quests.brief: Read the school notice and find the missing page.

questions.prompt: When does the reading club start?
questions.note: The notice says the club starts at nine.
questions.passage: Reading club starts at nine in the school garden. Bring a book and a pencil.

questions.prompt: Complete the note: “Please bring a book and a ___.”
questions.note: The notice asks for a book and a pencil.
questions.passage: Reading club starts at nine in the school garden. Bring a book and a pencil.

questions.prompt: Thank Nắng for helping you.
questions.note: “Thank you for your help” is a complete, polite sentence.

zones.name: Little Words Café
zones.intro: The café has a table for everyone. Help our visitors feel welcome and we’ll find another page.

quests.title: One warm conversation
quests.brief: Order a drink and make a new friend.

questions.prompt: Ask for tea politely.
questions.answer: Could I have a tea, please?
options: Could I have a tea, please?
questions.note: “Could I have…” makes a polite request.

questions.prompt: Ask someone to join you.
questions.answer: Would you like to sit here?
questions.note: “Would you like to…” is a friendly invitation.

questions.prompt: Listen to the visitor. Which drink would they like?
questions.note: The visitor asks for orange juice.
questions.passage: I would like orange juice, please. It is a warm day.

quests.title: A table for two
quests.brief: Fix a misunderstanding and recover the café’s page.

questions.prompt: You didn’t hear the visitor. What can you say?
questions.note: Ask someone to repeat themselves politely.

questions.prompt: Complete: “Nice to ___ you!”
questions.note: We say “Nice to meet you” when meeting someone.

questions.prompt: Your friend is free after lunch. When should you meet?
questions.note: After lunch usually means in the afternoon.
questions.passage: I’m busy this morning, but I’m free after lunch. Let’s meet at the café.

zones.name: Sunrail Station
zones.intro: Our little ferry is waiting for its passengers. Can you help everyone find the right way?

quests.title: A ticket somewhere new
quests.brief: Read the signs and buy the right ticket.

questions.prompt: You want to go to Green Bay and come back. What ticket do you need?
questions.note: A return ticket includes the journey back.

questions.prompt: Which platform does the train leave from?
questions.note: The announcement names platform three.
questions.passage: The train to Green Bay leaves from platform three.

questions.prompt: Ask how much your ticket costs.
questions.answer: How much is a return ticket?
questions.note: Use “How much is…” to ask a price.

quests.title: The missing departure
quests.brief: Help a lost traveler reach the ferry.

questions.prompt: Which direction should the traveler take at the café?
questions.note: The directions say to turn left at the café.
questions.passage: Walk straight to the café. Turn left there. The ferry is next to the bridge.

questions.prompt: Complete: “The ferry is next ___ the bridge.”
questions.note: “Next to” means beside.

questions.prompt: The train is delayed. What does that mean?
questions.note: “Delayed” means later than planned.

zones.name: Word Conservatory
zones.intro: Words grow better together. Match the right meanings and help this greenhouse bloom.

questions.prompt: Which word means nearly the same as “begin”?
questions.note: “Begin” and “start” are synonyms.

questions.prompt: Which word completes “___ a decision”?
questions.note: The common collocation is “make a decision”.

questions.prompt: Write the opposite of “empty”.
questions.note: “Full” is the opposite of “empty”.

quests.title: The page that blooms
quests.brief: Use context to restore a lost sentence.

questions.prompt: What does “tiny” mean here?
questions.note: The seed fits on a fingertip, so it is very small.
questions.passage: The tiny seed fit on the tip of my finger.

questions.prompt: Put the words into a sentence.
questions.answer: Small steps lead to big changes.
questions.note: The plural subject “steps” takes “lead”.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural phrase.
questions.note: “Heavy rain” is the usual collocation.

zones.name: Pencilworks Studio
zones.intro: We’re building a reading bench for the whole village. Clear words will help us work together.

quests.title: Make a plan together
quests.brief: Help Sỏi explain the team’s next steps.

questions.prompt: Explain what you are working on.
questions.answer: I am working on the design.
questions.note: Use the present continuous for work in progress.

questions.prompt: You need a clearer deadline. What do you ask?
questions.note: This question asks when the work should be ready.

questions.prompt: What should the team finish first?
questions.note: Sỏi asks the team to finish the design first.
questions.passage: Let’s finish the design first. We can choose the paint tomorrow.

quests.title: A promise you can keep
quests.brief: Negotiate a deadline and recover the studio’s page.

questions.prompt: You cannot finish by Friday. Choose a helpful response.
questions.answer: Could we move the deadline to Monday?
options: Could we move the deadline to Monday?
questions.note: Suggest a specific alternative when negotiating.

questions.prompt: Complete: “Thanks for your ___.” (being patient)
questions.note: “Thanks for your patience” acknowledges someone’s understanding.

questions.prompt: What is the team’s agreed plan?
questions.note: Sỏi accepts Monday as the revised delivery date.
questions.passage: Mây: Can we deliver on Monday instead? Sỏi: Yes, Monday works. Please send the design today.

zones.name: Recall Amphitheatre
zones.intro: Welcome to the village word festival. There’s no rush: a clear answer is better than a quick guess.

quests.title: The word festival
quests.brief: Use everything you have practiced so far.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
questions.answer: She goes to work by train.
options: She go to work by train.
She goes to work by train.
questions.note: Use “goes” with the subject “she”.

questions.prompt: Complete: “I ___ a decision yesterday.”
questions.note: The past tense of “make” is “made”.

questions.prompt: Invite a friend to the festival.
questions.answer: Would you like to come with us?
questions.note: “Would you like to…” offers an invitation.

quests.title: A festival for everyone
quests.brief: Read, listen and reason to earn the festival page.

questions.prompt: Why is the festival moving indoors?
questions.note: The announcement explains that rain caused the move.
questions.passage: Because it is raining, today’s word festival will be held inside the school.

questions.prompt: Which event takes place first?
questions.note: The welcome talk starts at ten, before the other events.
questions.passage: 10:00 Welcome talk. 10:30 Word game. 12:00 Village picnic.

questions.prompt: Your teammate makes a mistake. What is supportive?
questions.answer: Let’s try that one again together.
options: Let’s try that one again together.
questions.note: Encouragement makes teamwork and learning easier.

zones.name: Sunpage Lighthouse
zones.intro: Six pages have brought us here. Read carefully, listen closely, and help the village finish its story.

questions.prompt: What can you infer about the old bus service?
questions.note: A rise in frequency means buses ran less often before.
questions.passage: The town increased bus frequency from once an hour to every fifteen minutes.

questions.prompt: Complete: “The number of visitors has ___.” (gone up)
questions.note: “Increased” means gone up or become larger.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker recommend?
questions.note: The speaker recommends public transport to reduce traffic.
questions.passage: To reduce traffic in the village, I recommend taking public transport whenever possible.

quests.title: The story we made
quests.brief: Recover the final page and light the village storybook.

questions.prompt: Which sentence summarizes the message?
questions.answer: Small habits can make a lasting difference.
options: Small habits can make a lasting difference.
questions.note: The text emphasizes consistent short practice.
questions.passage: Learning a little every day builds confidence over time. Even a short conversation can teach you something useful.

questions.prompt: Put the village’s final message in order.
questions.answer: Every little word opens a new world.
questions.note: The singular subject “word” takes “opens”.

questions.prompt: A new learner arrives. What do you say?
options: Come back when you are perfect.
questions.note: Welcoming another learner completes the village’s story.
